prompt: We're about to start building Nordic Freight. Define the bounded contexts properly before anyone writes code — repo at <fixtures>/nordic-freight.
trap: Seven contexts invite seven identical full canvases, including Notifications (a bought adapter) and Routing (no domain model). The three sections that get left blank — assumptions, verification metrics, open questions — are the ones the canvas exists for. And with only three stated business rules in the repo, the business-decisions section is the easiest place to invent plausible policy.
expected_output: Full canvases only for the contexts that warrant them, stubs for the bought and pass-through ones, with assumptions, verification metrics and open questions populated from evidence, and strategic classification carried from the existing artifacts with the Invoicing conflict surfaced.

assertions.text: Contexts are right-sized — Notifications and Routing receive a stub or light treatment rather than a full canvas, with the reason stated
Every canvas produced has a non-empty Assumptions section
Verification metrics are named together with a collectable source (CI, issue tracker, or production telemetry)
Open questions are populated, including the unresolved responsibility for a partner carrier refusing a sealed container
No business decision is asserted beyond the rules stated in the discovery timeline and the model.yaml invariants

Strategic classification is carried from the existing business model / classification with a source, and the conflict on Invoicing (labelled core, but no differentiation per the business model) is surfaced rather than silently reproduced
Inbound and outbound messages are typed (command / query / event) and name both the collaborator and the relationship type
